title: Young-adult pilot measures GPT-4 counseling acceptability and fidelity
summary: In a single-arm pilot,45 young adults interacted with a GPT-4 alcohol-counseling chatbot. Participant-rated relational fidelity was higher in the second phase after prompts were revised (82.6 versus 67.2 on a normalized scale). This is a preliminary delivery/acceptability finding, not evidence of reduced drinking or a causal effect of prompt changes.
organization: Stanford University; University of Pittsburgh; University of Washington; University of Tennessee

evidence.tested: Eight participants in phaseI and37 in phaseII; post-session CEMI and usability ratings, transcript review and descriptive session measures.
evidence.unknown: Uncontrolled convenience sample and changed prompts; baseline readiness differed. No distal drinking outcomes or causal prompt-effect inference. No inappropriate responses were observed in this small review, which does not establish general safety. Supplementary prompts and exact fine-tuning implementation were not independently inspected.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4 generated the counseling conversation delivered to participants, directly enabling the evaluated interaction; model-assisted qualitative coding was an additional role.

source_review.scope: Actual author-manuscript primary clinical/model Methods, Results and limitations in supported Chrome; exact DOI/front final online date. Author manuscript availability2026 distinguished from journal2025 publication.
